kind: assumed inputs; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository
label_convention: An artifact name or citation path taken from the repository is written with a space on each side of every slash, as in observed-input.json. The paths of the toy tree and of the transfer task are invented.

toy_rule.note: A made-up tree for practising the counting rule. The artifact, its path and every file are invented; the rule applied to them is the producer's, with its four exclusion pathspecs.

files.what: a program that loads the rule, building its path from two parts
the rule file itself, with its own path in a comment
a record in a folder the producer excludes
an old note under a folder named archived
a data file that writes the name with spaced slashes
a lesson that names the rule
the French translation of that lesson
files.content: La règle se trouve dans toy/rule.yaml.

what_if.note: Synthetic additions to the observed counts: each case adds tracked files outside the excluded folders, and none of these files exists. A file that 'lists every path' contains each distinct citation path once.

one_path_in_several_files.why: a lesson that names one path, and its two translations

what_if.policy_reading: The policy's ratio is LOLLI_n / max(ERGOL_n, 1). Here citations_n is read literally from the policy's own source line, as the summed change of citation_count over the cycle; the three other components of ERGOL are set to 0; LOLLI_n is the number of files created, a catalogue file included. This reading is an assumption of the fixture, not a record of how the project applies the policy.

power_law_rule.note: The rule's population is its stated source: the citation_count of every evolution record, the two unmeasurable artifacts included (no added file can move their recorded counts). 20% of the artifacts is not a whole number of artifacts, so both readings are computed: floor (the most artifacts that are at most 20%) and ceil (the fewest that are at least 20%). The added files are synthetic: each names the citation paths of the measurable artifacts among the leaders, once each; a catalogue names every citation path once.

effort_model.note: Synthetic agents. Each has one unit of effort and puts it where its own reward is highest. Work yields a_i points of real value, which show one for one in the proxy. Inflation yields g_i proxy points and no value. The proxy also carries a measurement error. An agent's reward is (1 - w) x value + w x proxy, so it inflates when w x g_i > a_i. Every combination of the levels below is one equally likely kind of agent.

sample.draw: for each agent, three calls of random.Random(seed).random(): the work yield, the inflation yield, the proxy error; each value u picks the level at index floor(u x number of levels)

reflexive_forecast.note: Synthetic. A forecast of an artifact's citation count is published. If it is published in a tracked file that names the path literally, the forecast is itself a mention (self_mentions = 1). Readers may also react: for each point the forecast lies above the count that would have occurred without it, they add 'reaction' mentions (negative: they hold back). outcome = baseline + self_mentions + reaction x (forecast - baseline). The reaction values are assumptions; no such reaction was observed.

hypothesis.note: Thresholds of the hypothesis recorded in the research cycle before the what-if cases and the two models were run.

negative_controls.note: Changes planted in a copy of the observed input, to show that the checks react.

transfer_task.note: A hypothetical team wiki. It is not Streeling data and not a forecast. Counting rule of the wiki: a handbook's link count is the number of wiki pages that contain the handbook's address as a literal string, outside the folder trash; the handbook's own page is not counted.

pages.what: a runbook whose steps follow the east handbook; it calls it 'the east handbook' and gives no address
pages.content: Follow the east handbook, section 3, before each release.

pages.what: an index page that lists the five addresses
an older index page, moved to the trash folder
the east handbook's own page, which repeats its address in the footer

transfer_task.review_rule: every handbook with 0 links is put up for removal

ratio_rule.formula: new pages in the month / max(new links in the month, 1)
